Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 2442 of 2023

Appellant :- Ved Prakash @ Guddu
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Appellant :- Praveen Kumar Singh,Dewansh Singh
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Ajay Pratap Singh,Lal Mani Singh
Hon'ble Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra,J.

Heard learned counsel for the appellant, Sri Lal Mani Singh, learned counsel for the informant,
learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

Instant criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of SC/ST (P.A.) Act has been filed against the order dated 10.2.2023 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Allahabad in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.8238 of 2022, arising out of Case Crime No.438 of 2021, (S.S.T. No.375 of 2022),
under Sections 376(2)(n), 504, 506 IPC & Sections- 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (PA) Act, Police Station- Karchhana, District- Prayagraj.

On 4.11.2021 at around 9:00 P.M., when she was alone,
the accused and his one companion namely, Om Prakash @ Tinku had also maintained physical relationship with her and thereafter both had escaped from the place.

No.20475 of 2022 (Pooja Bhartiya vs. State of U.P. and 3 others) before this Court wherein she made a prayer to this effect that the State-respondents may be directed to produce her before courts below - C.J.M. Prayagraj to record her second statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. in connection with Case Crime No.438 of 2021, under Sections 376D, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2) (v) SC/ST Act, Police Station- Karchana, District- Prayagraj and this Court vide order dated 3.8.2022 summoned the first statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and finally disposed off the application vide order dated 15.11.2022 to this effect that "Now, the victim claims that she has got more to state in her statement which she intended at that point of time when her statement was previously recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of above, this much is observed that things may be looked by the Investigating Officer and he may take appropriate steps for ensuring fair investigation."
The second statement of prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 23.12.2022, wherein she stated that she aged about 21 years.
She is not educated.
The FIR in this case was lodged at the instance of Gram Pradhan.
She intended to rectify her previous statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. because that statement was given by her on pressure and threatening of her parents.
This is her last statement.
She named Om Prakash @ Tinku at the behest of Gram Pradhan namely, Pappu.
Learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that presently the accused and victim are willing to get themselves married after release of appellant from jail.
He lastly submitted that the appellant is not having any prior criminal history and that fact has specifically been stated in paragraph No.20 of the affidavit filed in support of the criminal appeal.
The learned court below has rejected the bail application of the appellant on insufficient grounds.
The case of the appellant for the purpose of bail was not duly considered by learned court below.
Learned counsel for the informant did not dispute the factual contentions raised by learned counsel for the appellant, which is based on record.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant and submitted that the victim supported the allegations in FIR and in her statements recorded under Sections 161 as well as 164 Cr.P.C.
She appears to be lying under influence of the accused side and she is trying to exonerate the appellant by way of her second statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

Considering the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties, facts and circumstances of the case,
nature of the offence, second statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for bail.
Accordingly, the appeal is hereby allowed.
The impugned order dated 10.2.2023 rejecting the bail application of the appellant is hereby set aside.

Let the appellant- Ved Prakash @ Guddu be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-

2 (i) That the appellant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) That the appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the appellant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned before the release of the appellant on bail.
It is made clear that in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the appellant.

It is also made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
